_comment: Reviewed-and-declined discovery candidates — repos a human evaluated via the curation discovery digest and chose NOT to adopt as a vendor skill (e.g. a moat-encroachment whose best idea was absorbed into the foundation's own rules, or an off-stack skill). curation-discover.sh excludes these repo-roots from the candidate set (declined_set, the discovery analogue of known_set) so a standing decision is never re-surfaced — as a proposal OR a moat signal — on every run. DISTINCT from registry.json (active vendor pins), awaiting-vendors.json (graduation veille), and presets' recommendedVendorSkills[].

entries.reason: Moat-encroachment: a stack-agnostic YAGNI / minimal-code 'lazy senior dev' methodology that competes with the foundation's own workflow/discipline layer (vendor-precedence tier 2 — the foundation owns how-we-work). Its best idea was ABSORBED into .claude/rules (the 7-rung minimal-code ladder) rather than adopted as a vendor skill.
Duplicate: the Prisma ORM codebase itself, not an agent skill. dev-prisma already points at the vendor's own skills repo (prisma/skills, registry).
A link catalogue of self-hosted apps, not a skill: nothing to install or follow. Same fit gate that rejected the other awesome-lists of the same run; this fit-4 verdict was the outlier.
Overlaps dev-frontend-design, which already points at the tool maker's own frontend-design skill (anthropics/claude-code plugin). Vendor-vs-vendor: authority over community (vendor-precedence).
